title: Sell Mineral Rights in Moundsville, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Moundsville, WV
metaDescription: Moundsville, Marshall County minerals: county-seat courthouse access, dense Marcellus/Utica units, and stacked-pay royalty questions.
heroLead: Moundsville is the Marshall County seat and sits in some of the densest Marcellus and Utica development in the state.
intro: As the county seat, Moundsville holds the Marshall County Courthouse and its full deed, will, and lease record — the reference point for tracing any mineral interest in this part of the county, whether it's under a legacy vertical well or a modern horizontal unit.

sections.heading: Working from the county seat's records
paragraphs: Because the courthouse is local, tracts around Moundsville have relatively accessible title records compared to more rural parts of Marshall County — though accessible doesn't mean simple, given how many leases and assignments have layered onto this acreage over decades of active development.

sections.heading: Dense unit development and stacked-pay potential
paragraphs: Moundsville sits in some of Marshall County's most heavily developed Marcellus and Utica/Point Pleasant acreage, with large pooled units common and stacked-pay development a real possibility for many tracts. Owners here should confirm both their unit percentage and whether their interest covers one formation or two before valuing it.

sections.heading: Confirming your interest before an operator's next unit filing
paragraphs: Given how frequently new units are permitted around Moundsville, it's worth periodically checking whether your tract has been swept into a filing you haven't been notified about — operators aren't always prompt about updating every mineral owner's contact information, particularly for interests with a long inheritance history.

A courthouse check cross-referencing your deed against recent pooling orders filed at the Marshall County Courthouse will confirm your current unit participation, whether or not you've received a division order reflecting it yet.

faqs.question: Is Moundsville a good place to find historical deed records for my interest?
faqs.answer: Yes — as the Marshall County seat, its courthouse holds the full local deed and lease record, making it the starting point for tracing your chain of title.

faqs.question: How dense is drilling around Moundsville?
faqs.answer: Among the densest in the state, with large pooled horizontal units and stacked-pay Marcellus/Utica development common in this part of Marshall County.

faqs.question: Could I have two separate royalty streams on one Moundsville-area tract?
faqs.answer: It's possible if the tract is developed for both the Marcellus and the deeper Utica/Point Pleasant under separate unit orders.

faqs.question: How often should I check whether my Moundsville tract has entered a new unit?
faqs.answer: Periodically, especially if you know drilling activity has picked up nearby — operators don't always promptly update every owner's contact record.

faqs.question: Should I expect a large or small pooled unit near Moundsville?
faqs.answer: Given the density of development in this part of Marshall County, large multi-tract units are common, so check the actual filed plat rather than assuming based on your original tract's size alone.
